title: Blowout: Comets buried by 34 in the fourth
arc: cold-open fury that deflates into a post-mortem — hot early, analytical late

lines.text: One eighteen to ninety-seven. Section 122 paid ninety dollars a seat for that, and they were filing out with nine minutes left in the third.
Thirty-four to thirteen in the fourth quarter, Bernie. Thirty-four to thirteen. Say it out loud and try not to wince.
Welcome to the show, everybody. Tonight we are performing an autopsy, and the body is still warm.
And unlike most autopsies, the cause of death is not a mystery. We watched it happen possession by possession.
They quit, Dutch. I am not supposed to say that on the air, but there is no other word. Grown professionals stopped running back on defense.
Eight straight empty possessions to open the fourth. Eight! You could hear the building change its mind in real time.
And the bench! The bench was sitting there like they were waiting for a bus. Nobody stood up once in twelve minutes.
That is the loudest silence in sports, the bench that has already accepted the result with six minutes left.
Now let us cool down and look at the film, because the collapse started way before the fourth. The spacing was broken from the opening tip.
Fine, yes, the corner was empty all night. Every drive collapsed into three defenders because nobody held the weak side.
And the switching scheme asked the big man to live on an island against guards. Somebody drew that up on a whiteboard in September and never took it back down.
So the effort died because the plan was already dead. That is the most damning version of this, honestly.
The schedule does them no favors. Three road games against top-five offenses in the next eight days.
If they show up flat Thursday, then this is who they are. And I will say it Thursday night, on this microphone, at eleven.
And that is the quiet part of a blowout. It does not just cost you a game, it asks a question about the whole roster.
We will be watching the answer on Thursday. That is the show. Go hug your bench players, folks.
